title: Data residency & region pinning - Security review
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed region pinning and data residency options for EU/US separation. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS options including BYOK/HSM, and sub-processor/cross-border processing controls. Customer asked about guarantees for EU-only processing, network egress, and how fallbacks to hosted models are handled. Agreed to share security whitepaper, SCCs and a proposed network architecture diagram, and to schedule a pilot for EU-only dedicated capacity.
action_items: Alex Morgan: Share Redwood security whitepaper, SOC 2 and ISO artifacts (redacted) - due 2025-04-14
Priya Shah: Provide proposed network architecture diagram for EU-only dedicated deployment and sample SCCs - due 2025-04-16
Marco Silva: Share Finova's list of required sub-processors and any contractual language for data residency - due 2025-04-18
next_steps: Send SOC 2/ISO redacted artifacts and security whitepaper
Schedule an architecture deep-dive (SE-led) for EU dedicated pilot
Prepare pricing/commit proposal for Dedicated EU capacity
Exchange SCCs and KMS integration details
transcript:
00:00 Alex Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate it. We've got about 40 minutes, uh - today is focused on your data residency and region pinning questions. Priya and I will run through architecture and certs.
00:12 Lena Ortiz: thanks Alex, yeah we've got a few people on the line, Marco and Rita, we want to make sure our payment data doesn't leave the EU. Can you confirm options for EU-only processing?
00:25 Priya Shah: absolutely. So there are two main paths: hosted with region pinning for EU-only routing, or Dedicated/Private where workloads run on reserved capacity provisioned in your EU region. Hosted is faster to start, but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees about where compute occurs.
00:45 Marco Silva: when you say hosted with region pinning, is that a hard guarantee? we can't have tokens or k-v cache going to us zones.
00:55 Priya Shah: good question. For hosted, we use regional endpoints and routing policies to prefer EU capacity. We also have contractual controls and network egress restrictions but hosted can fall back to nearby capacity if EU capacity is exhausted unless you choose a Dedicated EU pool which is physically isolated. There is some nuance: the control plane may still be in another region unless you opt for Private with a customer-managed control plane.
01:22 Lena Ortiz: so control plane metadata might move? that's a dealbreaker for us for certain data fields, is there documentation?
01:30 Alex Morgan: we'll share our security whitepaper and a note on what metadata is considered control plane only - e.g., billing/usage signals vs. payload. For strict EU-only requirements, we recommend Dedicated (or Private) with EU-only region pinning and contract language.
01:44 Marco Silva: ok, and sub-processors - which clouds and CDNs might be involved? we need a list for our vendor review.
01:52 Priya Shah: primary infra providers are AWS - eu-west-1 and GCP - europe-west1 for EU; we also partner with a logging subprocessor for long-term retention in some cases. We'll provide the up-to-date sub-processor list and SCCs. Note: some services, like global monitoring, may involve metadata in non-EU regions unless you choose Private.
02:14 Rita Chen: what about Schrems II and SCCs? we need assurances about lawful transfer mechanism.
02:20 Alex Morgan: we support SCCs and standard contractual clauses. For customers requiring additional controls, we offer contractual commitments and in some cases bespoke data processing addenda. We'll include sample SCC language for review.
02:33 Marco Silva: encryption, BYOK? we have strict key custody rules.
02:37 Priya Shah: we support BYOK via KMS integrations; you can use AWS KMS in your account or bring keys through an HSM. Keys never leave customer-managed HSM if you choose that option. For hosted customers we offer managed KMS with customer-supplied keys and rotation policies; for Dedicated/Private you can enable KMS in your VPC.
02:58 Marco Silva: rotation and key escrow protocols? and do you store plaintext anywhere?
03:03 Priya Shah: plaintext is not persisted by our service beyond transient memory during inference; we encrypt at rest with AEAD, and in transit via TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. Keys are used to wrap model artifacts on disk. We can supply whitepaper sections on key lifecycle and cryptographic controls.
03:23 Lena Ortiz: audit logs — does Redwood provide immutable audit logs that show who called what model, and can we push logs to our SIEM?
03:33 Alex Morgan: yes. We expose detailed audit logs including request IDs, model version, route, user token (hashed), timestamps and outcome. Logs can be forwarded via secure syslog or to customer s3/GCS buckets in EU. Retention can be configured; standard is 90 days in-hosted but we can accommodate longer retention for Dedicated and Private deployments.
03:55 Marco Silva: retention and deletion proofs — can you provide proof of deletion of backups?
04:01 Priya Shah: we provide deletion reports for customer-managed storage. For hosted we provide contractual deletion commitments and can run processes to scrub cached prefixes but we should scope that in the DPA.
04:12 Rita Chen: what about RBAC and SSO for team access to the console and logs?
04:17 Alex Morgan: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access control. We have predefined roles and custom roles for least privilege. We also support MFA via your IdP.
04:33 Marco Silva: any chance of cross-border caching? I'm thinking of kv cache and prefix cache.
04:40 Priya Shah: cache is region-specific for Dedicated EU pools. For hosted, prefix caching is regional but we have global caches for some models; we can disable cross-region caching for EU-only deployments.
04:53 Unk Speaker - contractor: (muffled) sorry if i jump in — how do you handle fallbacks if EU capacity is full mid-incident?
04:59 Priya Shah: in default hosted mode we have automated fallbacks to nearby capacity to maintain availability. For EU-only strict SLAs you should choose Dedicated with reserved capacity and can configure fallback policies — e.g., fail closed (reject) or fail open (route to compatible model in another region). We recommend fail-closed for regulated data.
05:20 Lena Ortiz: what's the SLA behavior — do you provide a credit if you route outside region?
05:26 Alex Morgan: contractual terms can include credits and penalties; we handle on a case-by-case basis in enterprise contract. We'll propose language for the Dedicated EU pilot.
05:36 Rita Chen: about model artifacts — are your model weights stored in region? where is the model hosted?
05:42 Priya Shah: model artifacts can be pinned to EU-only storage for Dedicated or Private. For hosted catalog models, our copies are region-replicated; we can provide EU-only model storage for enterprise customers subject to model licensing.
06:00 Marco Silva: what about sub-processors like analytics provider that may be US-based?
06:06 Alex Morgan: we will provide the sub-processor list and specific commitments. For workloads that cannot have US-based subprocessors, Private (customer-managed control plane) is the recommended approach.
06:18 Lena Ortiz: is there an attestation for SOC 2 / ISO? we need last audit date and scope.
06:23 Alex Morgan: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. We'll share the attestation dates and scope; redacted reports are available under NDA.
06:34 Marco Silva: can you also show proof around pen tests and vulnerability management cadence?
06:38 Priya Shah: yes, we publish pen test summaries and vulnerability management KPIs. We'll include those in the package.
06:45 Rita Chen: regarding legal, we need specific DPA language about cross-border processing and subprocessors — can you accept our standard clause?
06:53 Alex Morgan: we're used to negotiating DPAs; we'll take a look and propose edits. For critical deviations, our legal team will follow up.
07:02 Marco Silva: network egress and telemetry — will any telemetry (metrics, traces) leave EU?
07:09 Priya Shah: by default metrics are aggregated in-region but certain global monitoring tooling may ship anonymized metrics to central monitoring. For Dedicated/Private we can keep telemetry in-region and push to your endpoints. We'll provide a telemetry map.
07:24 Lena Ortiz: can you provide a diagram that shows the entire data flow: client -> region endpoint -> model compute -> storage -> logs?
07:30 Priya Shah: yes, we'll share a diagram and specifically annotate where data is encrypted and where keys live.
07:36 Alex Morgan: quick note on model fallbacks: if you choose a pinned model and it becomes unavailable, the platform can be configured to either reject requests (fail-closed) or route to a fallback model. We'll document default behavior and ways to lock down failover.
07:54 Rita Chen: for BYOK, do you support customer key rotation schedules and can we revoke keys if needed?
07:59 Priya Shah: yes, revocation is supported; we recommend a coordinated rotation plan. For HSM, key material never leaves your HSM. For managed keys, we offer KMS access controls with granular IAM.
08:12 Unk Speaker - contractor: ty, also do you support data residency for embeddings? we don't want customer embedding vectors to be processed outside EU.
08:19 Priya Shah: embeddings are treated like any other payload and can be scoped to EU-only compute and storage. We also have additional controls to anonymize or hash tokens before storing embeddings if needed.
08:33 Marco Silva: latency concerns — if we lock capacity in EU-only pool, does that increase cost?
08:39 Alex Morgan: usually Dedicated EU pools have higher unit costs due to capacity reservation and potential lower oversubscription. But you get predictable latency and no cross-border egress. We'll include cost estimates in the proposal.
08:52 Lena Ortiz: ok, happy with that. last question: are there any cases where you would be compelled to hand over data to non-EU authorities?
08:58 Alex Morgan: Redwood is bound by the law of the jurisdictions we operate in; for Private deployments where control plane and infrastructure are customer-managed, the risk is minimal. We'll add standard legal language and escalation processes.
09:12 Rita Chen: sounds good, let's get the docs and a proposed pilot.
09:15 Alex Morgan: great, we will send the package by next week. Thanks everyone.
09:20 (end of recording)
notes: Customer strongly prefers Dedicated EU pool or Private deployment for strict data residency. Key interests: BYOK/HSM, audit log forwarding to EU storage, SCCs, and fail-closed fallback policy. SE to propose architecture and pilot plan.
crm_notes: Opportunity flagged for enterprise pilot. Security gating on DPA and BYOK. Likely to convert to Dedicated with 12-month commit if pilot successful.
